description: An introduction to crop diseases covering their meaning, causal agents, symptoms, modes of spread, common examples in Tanzania, and methods of control.

mcq.questionText: What is the best definition of a crop disease?

options.text: Any insect that bites a crop plant
A harmful condition that disturbs the normal functioning of a crop plant
The normal drying of leaves during the dry season
The natural ripening of fruits on a plant

mcq.explanation: A crop disease is an abnormal condition that interferes with the normal growth, structure or function of a plant, usually reducing yield.

mcq.questionText: Which group of organisms causes the largest number of crop diseases?
mcq.explanation: Fungi are responsible for the greatest number of plant diseases, causing problems such as rusts, mildews, smuts and rots.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a viral disease of crops?
mcq.explanation: Cassava mosaic disease is caused by a virus and is spread mainly by whiteflies and infected cuttings.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is NOT a living (biotic) cause of crop disease?
mcq.explanation: Fungi, bacteria and viruses are living pathogens, while a shortage of nutrients is a non-living (abiotic) cause of disorders.

mcq.questionText: A common general symptom of a fungal leaf disease is:

options.text: Spots or patches on the leaves

mcq.explanation: Many fungal diseases show as coloured spots, patches or powdery growth on leaves and stems.

mcq.questionText: Which symptom describes 'wilting' in a diseased crop?

options.text: Plant parts drooping and losing firmness
Roots spreading widely in the soil

mcq.explanation: Wilting is the drooping and loss of firmness of leaves and stems, often because water movement in the plant is blocked.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common way crop diseases spread from plant to plant?

options.text: Through wind, water, insects and infected planting material
Only through the smell of flowers

mcq.explanation: Pathogens are spread by agents such as wind, water (rain splash and irrigation), insects, tools, and infected seeds or cuttings.

mcq.questionText: Using clean, disease-free seed bought from a recognised supplier is called using:
mcq.explanation: Certified seed has been inspected and approved as healthy and true to type, reducing the risk of introducing disease.

mcq.questionText: Which control method uses chemicals such as fungicides to manage crop disease?
mcq.explanation: Chemical control involves applying substances such as fungicides or bactericides to kill or limit pathogens.

mcq.questionText: Crop rotation helps control disease mainly because it:

options.text: Breaks the life cycle of pathogens that attack one crop
Removes all insects from the farm
Stops rain from falling on the field

mcq.explanation: By changing the crop grown on a piece of land, pathogens that depend on a particular host lose their food and decline.

mcq.questionText: Removing and burning diseased plant remains from the field is an example of:
mcq.explanation: Field hygiene includes clearing and destroying infected material so that the pathogen does not survive and re-infect the next crop.

mcq.questionText: A 'resistant variety' is a crop type that:

options.text: Is able to withstand or resist attack by a particular disease
Always needs more chemicals than other crops

mcq.explanation: Resistant varieties have a natural ability to tolerate or fight off certain diseases, reducing losses and the need for chemicals.

mcq.questionText: Which pair correctly matches a pathogen group with a type of crop disease?
mcq.explanation: Rusts such as maize rust and coffee leaf rust are caused by fungi; cassava mosaic is viral and bacterial wilt is bacterial.

mcq.questionText: Why is it risky for a farmer to take planting cuttings from an obviously diseased cassava plant?

options.text: The new plants may carry and pass on the same disease
The cuttings cannot be planted in the rainy season
The cuttings always produce sweeter tubers

mcq.explanation: Diseases such as cassava mosaic can be carried in cuttings, so using infected material spreads the disease to the new crop.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following BEST shows an integrated approach to controlling a crop disease?

options.text: Spraying chemicals only, very heavily, once a season
Combining resistant varieties, certified seed, crop rotation and field hygiene
Doing nothing and hoping the disease disappears
Planting the same infected crop every year

mcq.explanation: Combining several methods (cultural, resistant varieties, clean seed and hygiene) gives more reliable, sustainable disease control than relying on one method alone.

fib.questionText: A condition that interferes with the normal functioning of a crop plant and reduces its yield is called a crop _____.
fib.explanation: A crop disease disturbs the normal structure or function of a plant, usually lowering production.

fib.questionText: Living organisms that cause diseases, such as fungi, bacteria and viruses, are known as _____.
fib.explanation: Pathogens are disease-causing organisms that attack and harm crop plants.

fib.questionText: The group of pathogens responsible for rusts, mildews and smuts in crops is the _____.
fib.explanation: Fungi cause the largest number of crop diseases, including rusts and mildews.

fib.questionText: Cassava mosaic disease is caused by a _____.
fib.explanation: Cassava mosaic is a viral disease spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings.

fib.questionText: The drooping and loss of firmness in leaves and stems of a sick plant is a symptom called _____.
fib.explanation: Wilting often occurs when the movement of water in the plant is blocked by a disease.

fib.questionText: Insects such as whiteflies and aphids that carry pathogens from one plant to another are called disease _____.
fib.explanation: A vector is an organism that transmits a pathogen from an infected plant to a healthy one.

fib.questionText: Seed that has been inspected and approved as healthy and true to type is known as _____ seed.
fib.explanation: Certified seed reduces the chance of introducing diseases into a field.

fib.questionText: Growing different crops on the same piece of land in successive seasons to break pest and disease cycles is called crop _____.
fib.explanation: Crop rotation starves host-specific pathogens by changing the crop grown each season.

fib.questionText: Spraying a crop with a chemical called a _____ is used to control fungal diseases.
fib.explanation: Fungicides are chemicals that kill or stop the growth of disease-causing fungi.

fib.questionText: Keeping the farm clean by removing and destroying diseased plant remains is part of field _____.
fib.explanation: Field hygiene (sanitation) reduces the survival and spread of pathogens in a field.

tf.questionText: A crop disease always reduces the quality or quantity of yield from the affected plant.
tf.explanation: Diseases disturb normal plant functions, generally lowering yield and quality.

tf.questionText: All crop diseases are caused by insects.
tf.explanation: Diseases are caused by pathogens such as fungi, bacteria and viruses; insects mainly act as pests or vectors.

tf.questionText: Fungi cause more crop diseases than bacteria and viruses combined.
tf.explanation: Fungi are the most common cause of plant diseases, leading to rusts, mildews, smuts and rots.

tf.questionText: Viruses can be spread from one plant to another by insect vectors such as whiteflies.
tf.explanation: Many plant viruses, such as the cassava mosaic virus, are transmitted by sap-sucking insects.

tf.questionText: Yellowing of leaves, spots and stunted growth can be signs of a diseased crop.
tf.explanation: These are common general symptoms shown by plants suffering from disease.

tf.questionText: Rain splash and irrigation water can help spread crop diseases.
tf.explanation: Water can carry spores and bacteria from infected plants to healthy ones.

tf.questionText: Planting resistant varieties is a way of controlling crop diseases.
tf.explanation: Resistant varieties can withstand attack by certain diseases, reducing losses.

tf.questionText: Using cuttings from a diseased plant is a safe way to avoid spreading disease.
tf.explanation: Infected cuttings carry the pathogen and pass the disease to the new plants.

tf.questionText: Fungicides are chemicals used to control bacterial diseases only.
tf.explanation: Fungicides control fungal diseases; bactericides are used against bacteria.

tf.questionText: Crop rotation can help reduce the build-up of disease-causing organisms in the soil.
tf.explanation: Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of host-specific pathogens.

summary.correctAnswer: A harmful condition that disturbs the normal functioning of a crop and reduces yield.
summary.explanation: It is an abnormal state of the plant caused mainly by pathogens or poor conditions.
These living pathogens infect plants and cause most crop diseases.
Fungi cause the greatest number of crop diseases, such as rusts and mildews.

summary.questionText: Common symptoms of a diseased plant
summary.correctAnswer: Leaf spots, yellowing, wilting, stunted growth and rotting.
summary.explanation: These visible signs show that a plant is suffering from disease.

summary.correctAnswer: Wind, water, insects, tools and infected seeds or cuttings.
summary.explanation: Pathogens move between plants through these agents.

summary.questionText: Example of a viral crop disease
summary.explanation: It is caused by a virus and spread by whiteflies and infected cuttings.

summary.questionText: Example of a fungal crop disease
summary.explanation: Rusts are caused by fungi and appear as coloured spots on leaves.

summary.correctAnswer: Crop rotation, proper spacing, timely planting and field hygiene.
summary.explanation: These farming practices reduce conditions that favour disease.

summary.correctAnswer: It is healthy and disease-free, reducing the risk of introducing disease.
summary.explanation: Certified seed is inspected and approved before sale.

summary.correctAnswer: They withstand certain diseases, lowering losses and the need for chemicals.
summary.explanation: Resistant crops have a natural ability to tolerate specific diseases.

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that maize plants in one part of the field are wilting and dying in patches that slowly enlarge, while neighbouring fields planted with a different crop are healthy. Which explanation and action is MOST appropriate?

options.text: The problem is normal ripening, so no action is needed
A soil-borne disease may be present; the farmer should remove affected plants and practise crop rotation
The healthy fields prove there is no disease anywhere
The farmer should plant the same maize on that spot again immediately

hoq.explanation: Spreading patches of wilting suggest a soil-borne pathogen; removing infected plants and rotating crops helps break its cycle.

hoq.questionText: A region suffers heavy losses from a viral disease spread by an insect vector. Which combination of measures would give the most effective long-term control?

options.text: Planting resistant varieties, using clean planting material and controlling the insect vector
Only spraying fungicide on the leaves
Ignoring the vector and relying on rainfall

hoq.explanation: Because the disease is viral and insect-spread, resistant varieties, disease-free planting material and vector control together are most effective; fungicides do not kill viruses.

hoq.questionText: Two farmers grow the same crop. Farmer A reuses seed from last year's diseased harvest and plants densely; Farmer B uses certified seed, proper spacing and clears old crop debris. Why is Farmer B likely to have less disease?

options.text: Because certified seed and spacing reduce sources of infection and limit how easily disease spreads
Because dense planting always protects crops from disease
Because reusing diseased seed removes all pathogens
Because clearing debris increases pathogen survival

hoq.explanation: Clean certified seed removes a source of infection, good spacing reduces humid conditions and easy spread, and clearing debris limits pathogen survival.
